breakfast.name: Bake and Saltfish
instructions: Make bake dough, rest
Fry bakes until golden and puffy
Sauté flaked saltfish with onion, tomato, pepper
Serve bakes stuffed with saltfish
breakfast.description: Puffy fried bake with seasoned salt cod.

breakfast.name: Pholourie
instructions: Mix batter with spices
Drop spoonfuls in hot oil
Fry until golden
Serve with mango chutney
breakfast.description: Guyanese split pea fritters with mango chutney.

breakfast.name: Bake and Saltfish
ingredients: Bake (fried bread): flour, baking powder, sugar, salt, butter, water
Saltfish: salted cod (soaked overnight), onion, tomato, garlic, Scotch bonnet, thyme
instructions: Make bake dough: flour, baking powder, sugar, salt, butter — knead, rest 15 min
Shape into rounds, deep fry until puffed and golden — they inflate dramatically
For saltfish: soak overnight, boil briefly, flake into pieces
Sauté onion, tomato, garlic, Scotch bonnet, thyme, add flaked salt cod
Stir until heated through and flavors meld
Split the hot bake, stuff with saltfish mixture
The puff of the bake and the savory-salt hit of the fish is perfect morning food
Every Caribbean country has a version — Guyana's is among the most beloved
breakfast.description: Guyana's morning staple — puffy fried bread (bake) split and stuffed with sautéed salt cod. The dramatic puffing of the bake and the savory saltfish filling represent Caribbean breakfast at its most satisfying. Every Guyanese diaspora member craves bake and saltfish.

breakfast.name: Channa and Aloo (Curried Chickpeas and Potato)
ingredients: Curry powder (Guyanese — heavy on cumin and turmeric)
instructions: Heat oil, add cumin seeds — let them crackle
Sauté onion, garlic, add curry powder — fry until fragrant
Add potatoes, cook until starting to soften
Add chickpeas, Scotch bonnet, enough water to create a sauce
Simmer until potatoes are tender and sauce thickens
The sauce should coat the chickpeas and potatoes — not soupy
Serve with roti (flatbread) — tear roti and scoop
This is Indo-Guyanese comfort food — the Indian-Caribbean fusion at its best
breakfast.description: Indo-Guyanese curried chickpeas and potato — the Indian-Caribbean fusion that defines Guyana's food identity. The cumin-seed crackle, the curry-coconut aroma, and the roti-scooping technique represent the living Indian heritage in the Caribbean. Viral as one of the best examples of diaspora cuisine.

breakfast.name: Fry Bora and Saltfish
instructions: Soak saltfish overnight, boil, flake
Cut bora (long beans) into 2-inch pieces
Stir-fry bora until tender-crisp — 5 min
Add onion, garlic, tomato, Scotch bonnet
Add flaked saltfish, toss together
Season to taste
Serve with rice or roti for breakfast
The crunch of the bora against the salty fish is the hook
breakfast.description: Guyanese stir-fried long beans (bora) with saltfish — a morning staple that showcases the Indian-Caribbean technique of quick vegetable stir-fry. The yard-long beans bring a crunch that short green beans can't match.

lunch.name: Pepperpot
instructions: Brown meats
Add cassareep, spices, peppers
Cover with water, simmer 3 hours
Stew darkens and meat falls apart
Serve with bread
lunch.description: Guyana's national dish — a dark, complex meat stew preserved with cassareep.

lunch.name: Cook-Up Rice
ingredients: 1 cup pigeon peas or black-eyed peas
instructions: Cook salted meat until tender
Add rice, peas, coconut milk, spices
Cook covered until rice is done
lunch.description: One-pot rice with coconut milk and pigeon peas.

lunch.name: Pepperpot (Guyanese National Dish)
ingredients: Beef (shin, oxtail, or cow heel — tough cuts that benefit from long cooking)
Cassareep (essential — boiled-down cassava juice with spices, the soul of pepperpot)
instructions: Cut beef into large chunks — keep bones in
Add to a large pot with cassareep — the dark, sweet-bitter cassava extract is non-negotiable
Add cinnamon, cloves, orange peel, thyme, Scotch bonnet, brown sugar
Add water to cover, bring to a simmer
Cook low and slow for 3-4 hours until meat is fall-apart tender
The cassareep turns the stew almost black — the color is dramatic and beautiful
The sauce should be thick, glossy, and deeply complex — sweet, bitter, spicy, savory
Serve with homemade bread for soaking up the sauce
Pepperpot is a preservative stew — traditionally kept going for weeks, reheated daily with fresh meat added
This is Guyana's Christmas dish — no Christmas table is complete without pepperpot
lunch.description: Guyana's national dish — beef slow-cooked for hours in cassareep (boiled-down cassava juice), turning almost black and deeply complex. The ancient Amerindian preservation technique (cassareep acts as a preservative) means pepperpot can theoretically be kept going indefinitely, with fresh meat added daily. The 'eternal stew' concept and the dramatic black color are viral.

lunch.name: Cook-Up Rice (Guyanese One-Pot)
instructions: Soak salted meat overnight
Brown chicken and salted meat
Sauté onion, garlic, thyme
Add coconut milk, water, peas — cook until peas are almost tender
Add rice, stir once, cover tightly
Cook on low — do not lift the lid — until rice absorbs all liquid
The coconut milk makes the rice creamy and fragrant
Add cassava and plantain in the last 15 min if using
The bottom should be slightly crispy — the 'bun-bun'
This is Saturday food — every Guyanese household makes cook-up on Saturday
lunch.description: Guyana's Saturday tradition — rice, peas, and meat cooked together in coconut milk until the bottom layer caramelizes (the bun-bun, the prize serving). Similar to Caribbean pelau and West African jollof in concept but uniquely Guyanese. The Saturday ritual and the bun-bun fight make cook-up rice viral Guyanese food content.

lunch.name: Metemgee (Root Vegetable Coconut Stew)
ingredients: Root vegetables: cassava, eddoe, sweet potato, plantain (green and ripe)
instructions: Peel and cut all root vegetables into large chunks
Add to a pot with coconut milk — everything cooks in coconut
Add salted or smoked fish
Add dumplings — simple flour-and-water dumplings that cook in the stew
Simmer until all vegetables are tender and coconut milk thickens — 30-40 min
Season with thyme, garlic, Scotch bonnet
The stew should be thick and creamy from the coconut
Serve in deep bowls — each bowl gets a mix of every vegetable
This is Amerindian-origin cooking — the original inhabitants' gift to Guyanese cuisine
lunch.description: Guyana's Amerindian-heritage stew — root vegetables and dumplings simmered in coconut milk with smoked fish. A living link to the indigenous cooking of the Guyanese interior. The 'everything in coconut' approach and the Amerindian food-origin story make metemgee a viral piece of Caribbean food history.

lunch.name: Dhal Puri (Split Pea Stuffed Flatbread)
ingredients: Dough: flour, baking powder, oil, water
Filling: yellow split peas (cooked, ground), cumin, garlic, pepper
instructions: Cook split peas until soft, drain, grind coarsely with cumin and garlic
Make soft dough, rest 30 min
Divide dough into balls, flatten, add spoonful of ground split pea filling
Seal dough around filling, flatten gently, roll out thin without breaking
Cook on hot tawa (flat griddle) — brush with oil
The dhal puri should puff slightly, have golden spots, and be flaky
The filling should be visible as a thin layer inside — you can see it when you tear
This is the crown jewel of Indo-Caribbean bread — harder to make than roti, worth every minute
Serve with curry chicken, duck, or channa — wrap and eat with hands
lunch.description: The crown jewel of Indo-Guyanese flatbread — split peas ground with cumin and sealed inside dough, rolled thin, and cooked on a tawa. The visible dal layer inside the flaky bread is the sign of a master hand. Dhal puri is the bread that Indo-Caribbean grandmothers are famous for.

lunch.name: Hassar Curry (Armored Catfish)
ingredients: Hassar (armored catfish — bony, plated fish found in Guyana's rivers)
instructions: Clean hassar — the armor plates are the challenge, requires a specific technique
Cut into pieces, season with curry
Fry curry powder in oil until dark and fragrant
Add onion, garlic, add the hassar
Pour in coconut milk, add Scotch bonnet, thyme
Simmer 30-40 min until fish is tender
The thick coconut-curry sauce is the star — the fish adds body and umami
Eat carefully — the bones are many but the flavor is worth it
This is interior Guyana food — Amerindian-origin ingredients with Indo-Guyanese technique
lunch.description: Guyana's armored catfish curry — hassar, a prehistoric-looking plated catfish from the rivers of Guyana's interior, simmered in curry and coconut milk. The fusion of Amerindian ingredients with Indian technique makes hassar curry a uniquely Guyanese creation.

dinner.name: Curry Chicken Guyanese Style
instructions: Season chicken with curry and garlic
Brown in oil
Add potatoes, onion, pepper, water
Simmer 30 min until chicken is tender

dinner.name: Metemgee
instructions: Boil coconut milk
Add provisions: cassava, plantain, eddoe, dumplings
Add salted meat or fish
Cook until provisions are tender
dinner.description: Root vegetables and dumplings in thick coconut milk.

dinner.name: Curry Chicken (Guyanese Style)
ingredients: Curry powder (Guyanese — roasted, with heavy cumin and fenugreek)
instructions: Season chicken with curry powder, garlic, let marinate at least 30 min
Heat oil, add more curry powder — fry until fragrant and dark
Brown chicken in the curry oil
Add onion, potatoes, Scotch bonnet, thyme
Add water, simmer 30-40 min until chicken is tender and sauce is thick
The sauce should coat the chicken — not thin and soupy
The Guyanese curry is darker and more intensely spiced than Indian versions
Serve with paratha roti — tear roti and scoop curry
The curry stains everything yellow — this is how you know it's proper Guyanese curry
dinner.description: Guyanese curry chicken — darker, more intensely spiced than Indian curry, reflecting 180+ years of Indo-Caribbean evolution. The curry-stained-fingers and the roti-tearing technique are cultural markers. The 'Caribbean curry vs. Indian curry' comparison is a viral food discourse.

dinner.name: Garlic Pork
instructions: Cube pork, season with salt and all the garlic — the amount of garlic is extreme
Add vinegar, thyme, peppers, cloves
Marinate in the fridge for 3-7 days — the vinegar 'cooks' and preserves the pork
When ready, fry the marinated pork in its own fat until golden and crispy
The garlic becomes mellow and sweet from the long marination
Serve with bread or rice
This is a Portuguese-Guyanese Christmas tradition — the marination starts days before Christmas
The vinegar preservation technique means no refrigeration was originally needed
dinner.description: Guyanese-Portuguese Christmas pork — cubed pork marinated for days in vinegar, an insane amount of garlic, and hot peppers, then fried crispy. The week-long preparation and the 'that's too much garlic' (it's not) reaction make garlic pork viral every December in Guyanese food content.

dinner.name: Egg Ball
ingredients: Batter: flour, turmeric, curry powder, salt, water
instructions: Hard-boil eggs, peel
Make batter with flour, turmeric, curry powder, salt, water — thick enough to coat
Dip eggs in batter, ensuring complete coverage
Deep fry until golden and crispy — 3-4 min
The curry-turmeric batter becomes a golden, spiced shell around the egg
Serve with pepper sauce
These are Guyana's street food snack — sold at every roadside stall
Simple, cheap, satisfying — the Guyanese Scotch egg
dinner.description: Guyana's street snack — hard-boiled eggs coated in curry-turmeric batter and deep-fried into golden orbs. The Guyanese Scotch egg. Simple, cheap, and sold at every roadside stall. The golden curry shell and the cross-section reveal make egg balls viral Guyanese street food.

dinner.name: Duck Curry (Guyanese Style)
instructions: Season duck with curry, garlic, let marinate
Heat oil, fry curry powder until very dark — the 'burning' of the curry is key
Brown duck pieces in the curry oil
Add onion, potatoes, wiri wiri pepper, thyme
Add water (or coconut milk for richness)
Cover, cook low and slow 60-90 min — duck needs time to become tender
The fat from the duck enriches the curry — skim excess if you want, but it's flavor
The curry should be thick and dark — almost black from the burnt curry technique
Serve with dhal puri, roti, or rice — the duck fat-enriched curry demands good bread
dinner.description: Guyanese duck curry — dark, intense, slow-cooked. The 'burning' of the curry powder (frying until nearly black) is the technique that separates Guyanese curry from all others. Duck's richness stands up to the aggressive spicing. This is what Guyanese families cook for celebrations.

snacks.name: Egg Ball
instructions: Coat each egg in split pea batter
Deep fry until golden
snacks.description: Hard-boiled eggs wrapped in split pea dough, deep fried.

snacks.name: Pholourie (Fried Split Pea Dough Balls)
ingredients: Split pea flour (or ground yellow split peas)
instructions: Mix split pea flour with flour, turmeric, cumin, garlic, baking powder, water
Batter should be thick but spoonable
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil — they puff into round balls
Fry until deep golden — 3-4 min
Drain briefly
Serve with tamarind sauce (mango sour) — the tangy dip is essential
These are the snack of every Guyanese gathering — Hindu prayer meetings, parties, cricket matches
The puff and the tamarind dip are the hooks
snacks.description: Guyana's fried split-pea puffs — golden balls of spiced batter served with tangy tamarind sauce. Essential at every Hindu prayer meeting, cricket match, and party. The Indo-Guyanese tradition and the addictive puff-and-dip format make pholourie viral in Caribbean Indian food content.

snacks.name: Cassava Pone
instructions: Grate cassava and coconut — traditionally by hand, which is labor-intensive
Mix with brown sugar, melted butter, spices, vanilla, coconut milk
Add raisins if desired
Pour into a greased baking pan
Bake at 175°C for 50-60 min until firm and golden on top
The bottom and edges should be slightly caramelized
The texture is dense, moist, chewy — not cake, not pudding, uniquely pone
Let cool slightly — serve warm or at room temperature
Every Guyanese grandmother has THE recipe — and they all taste different
snacks.description: Guyanese cassava pone — grated cassava and coconut baked into a dense, sweet, chewy slab somewhere between cake and pudding. Every Guyanese grandmother's recipe is 'the' recipe. The hand-grating tradition and the unique texture make cassava pone viral Caribbean baking content.

desserts.name: Cassava Pone
instructions: Mix cassava, coconut, sugar, spices
Add coconut milk and butter
Pour into greased pan
Bake at 175°C 60 min
Cool and slice
desserts.description: Dense, sweet cassava and coconut bake.

desserts.name: Black Cake (Guyanese Christmas Cake)
ingredients: Dried fruits: raisins, currants, prunes, mixed peel — soaked in rum and port for MONTHS
instructions: Soak dried fruits in rum and port for minimum 2 weeks — traditional families start soaking months ahead
Make browning: caramelize sugar until almost burnt, very dark — this gives the cake its black color
Cream butter and brown sugar, add browning
Add eggs one at a time
Fold in flour and spices
Add the rum-soaked fruit purée (blend the soaked fruit) and extra rum
Pour into lined tins — the batter is very dark, almost black
Bake low and slow at 140°C for 2+ hours until firm
'Feed' the cake with more rum every few days until Christmas
The cake is jet black, dense, boozy, and keeps for months
This is Guyanese Christmas — no celebration without black cake
desserts.description: Guyana's legendary Christmas cake — dried fruits soaked in rum for MONTHS, baked with burnt sugar caramel until jet black, then 'fed' with more rum until Christmas. The months-long preparation, the black color, and the boozy density make Guyanese black cake the most extreme fruit cake in the world and perpetually viral at Christmas.

desserts.name: Mithai (Indian Sweets Guyanese Style)
instructions: Mix powdered milk with melted butter and sugar
Add cardamom — the defining spice
Add pink food coloring (traditional)
Cook mixture gently, stirring until it pulls together
Shape into small squares or diamonds while still warm
Let cool and set
These are Indo-Caribbean sweets — made for every Hindu celebration in Guyana
The cardamom and pink color are the signature
Simpler than Indian mithai but deeply nostalgic for Indo-Guyanese
desserts.description: Guyanese mithai — simplified Indian sweets made from powdered milk, butter, and cardamom, tinted traditional pink. Made for every Hindu celebration in Guyana, these sweets represent 180+ years of Indian heritage in the Caribbean. The pink color and cardamom scent are deeply nostalgic.

drinks.name: Mauby
instructions: Boil bark with spices 15 min
Strain, add sugar
Cool, let ferment slightly
Serve cold
drinks.description: Bittersweet bark drink — an acquired taste.

drinks.name: Swank (Plantain Drink)
instructions: Grate plantains into water
Add lime juice and sugar
Strain, serve cold with nutmeg

drinks.name: Mauby
instructions: Boil mauby bark with cinnamon, anise, orange peel, cloves for 15-20 min
Strain the dark, bitter liquid
Add sugar — lots, it needs to be sweet to balance the bitterness
Cool completely
The flavor is bitter-sweet — like root beer's Caribbean cousin
Some people ferment it slightly for a fizzy version
Chill — serve ice cold
The first sip is always a surprise for newcomers — the bitterness is unique
Mauby is an acquired taste — Guyanese and Trinidadians argue about whose is better
drinks.description: Mauby — the Caribbean's most polarizing drink. Dark bark tea sweetened and spiced, tasting like root beer's bitter Caribbean cousin. You either love it or you don't (yet). The bark-to-drink process and the 'first taste' reactions make mauby perpetually viral in Caribbean food content.
